section_summary.extract_value: This section reports hierarchical regression analyses conducted separately for women and men to test whether BAS predicts self-esteem beyond BES variables. For both genders the final models were significant, and BAS was the only significant predictor of self-esteem (women: β = -0.25, R^2 change = 4%; men: β = -0.27, R^2 change = 4%).
section_summary.evidence_source: "Hierarchical regressions were conducted with women and men separately to examine whether BAS predicts self-esteem above-and-beyond BES." "For women, the final regression model was significant [F(4,155) = 5.88,p < .001, adjusted R^2 = .11, but only BAS (β = -.25, t = -2.58, p < .05, R^2 = 4%) remained a significant predictor of self-esteem. Similarly for men, the final regression was significant [F(4,143) = 5.01, p < .05, adjusted R^2 = .10, with only BAS (β = -.27, t = -2.81, p < .05, R^2 = 4%) significantly predicting self-esteem.]"
